subject: Inference ops activation: sprint plan & cost/perf decisions
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@novaforge.io>, Alex Wu <alex.wu@novaforge.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Inference ops activation: sprint plan & cost/perf decisions

Hi Samira / Alex —

Great to kick this off. Per our discovery call, Novaforge has two distinct inference paths we need to tune during the activation sprint:

1) Realtime product recommendations (strict P99 latency target, higher cost tolerance)
2) Nightly batch embedding pipeline (throughput and unit-cost are the priority)

Goals for this thread: lock in the tuning decisions (batching, cache strategy, quantization profile choices, and routing/fallback policy) that we'll implement during the 3-week activation sprint starting 11/15.

Quick proposed plan (high level):
- Week 1: baseline instrumentation + sample workload ingest (you to provide representative payloads)
- Week 2: implement batching & prefix/KV caching patterns; run int8/int4 quant profiles for non-prod traffic
- Week 3: routing policy smoke tests, SLA validation, production rollout plan

Decisions we need from you by 11/11:
- Which path is strictest: latency or accuracy? (we heard latency for realtime)
- Will you accept an int8 quantized variant for realtime if it meets P99 SLOs?
- For nightly batches, are we allowed to run asynchronous quantization and aggressive batching?

I've attached a short integration-checklist and a sample JSON schema we need. Monica will own cache/prefetch design; Karthik will handle routing and model variant selection. I'll coordinate rollout and the HubSpot tasks.

Please reply with the workload sample link and confirm the decision on latency vs cost so we can lock profiles.

Thanks —
Sergio

Subject: Re: Inference ops activation: sprint plan & cost/perf decisions

Thanks, Sergio —

Confirming: realtime recommendations are the priority for user-facing latency (P99 <= 120ms goal). Nightly embedding job should be optimized for $/embedding and can be relaxed on latency.

On quantization: we prefer to keep realtime quality very close to baseline — if int8 keeps top-k accuracy within 1-2% we can accept it, otherwise we want int16 for the realtime model. Nightly jobs can be int8 or int4 if you demonstrate minimal drift.

I've uploaded a representative workload sample to our S3 (link below) and shared read access to your service account. The payload includes both small interactive requests (~30 tokens) and longer contextual requests (~700 tokens).

I'll be available for a 30-minute sync tomorrow (11/09) at 10:00 PT to walk through a few examples.

Samira

Head of ML Engineering, Novaforge
samira@novaforge.io

Date: 2026-11-08T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Inference ops activation: sprint plan & cost/perf decisions

Appreciate the clarity, Samira. That gives us a good axis to optimize along. Action items I captured:

- Novaforge: provide the S3 link (done) + any traffic distribution or session traces by 11/10 (Samira)
- Monica: design KV prefetch & expiration policy for realtime (deliverable 11/12)
- Karthik: propose routing policy with dedicated pool for realtime and fallback to quantized hosted variant (deliverable 11/13)
- Sergio: run an initial quant matrix (int16 / int8 / int4) against the sample workload and return a comparison report (deliverable 11/13)

Notes on quant profiles (initial thinking):
- int16-lowlatency: preserves most FP32 characteristics, small perf uplift, lower cost reduction
- int8-balanced: ~2-3x cost reduction on token generation, moderate latency improvement, slight NN accuracy drift
- int4-aggressive: large cost wins for batch jobs, less suitable for realtime unless paired with aggressive caching

Routing suggestion (draft):
- Route realtime traffic to Redwood Dedicated pool pinned to int16-lowlatency by default
- If queueing/latency spikes breach SLO, failover to hosted int8-balanced variant with adaptive batching disabled for single-request flows
- Batched embedding jobs route to a quantized cluster (int8 or int4) with larger batch windows

I've attached quant-profiles.csv (stub) and the updated integration checklist. I'll run the first matrix tonight and post results to the shared drive.

Sergio

Attachment(s): quant-profiles.csv, integration-checklist.xlsx

Subject: Re: Inference ops activation: sprint plan & cost/perf decisions

Quick note — I'll own the KV cache/prefetch design. Preliminary plan:
- Prefetch top-3 KV entries for active sessions; TTL 90s by default, adjustable after week-1 telemetry
- Separate cache for long-context requests (>=512 tokens) with a larger TTL but capped size to avoid blowup
- Add instrumentation hooks for cache hit/miss and per-request cache latency so we can tie to P99

I'll add these items as JIRA subtasks under the activation epic and share the links by COB 11/09. For routing, I support Karthik's default to Dedicated with hosted fallback; will add sticky routing header to keep session affinity where possible.

Monica
